summary: Transit Gateway GRE tunnel MTU blackhole causes TLS1.3 handshake to hang during large model/artifact pulls
description:
Issue summary: Customer's private deployment behind a Transit Gateway using GRE-based SD-WAN overlay reports intermittent hangs during model/artifact downloads. A subset of large pulls (range requests or downloads with large TLS records and OCSP/SNI extensions) stall during TLS1.3 handshake and the client eventually times out.
Impact: Serving nodes fail to fetch model shards affecting inference for a small percentage (~4%) of requests; customers see degraded QPS and elevated client-side timeouts.
Environment: Private deployment (VPCs peered via Transit Gateway), GRE encapsulation between branch SD-WAN and on-prem, VPCE for artifact access to S3 via a corporate egress appliance.
Steps to reproduce: 1) From a node inside the affected VPC, trigger a large model shard download (>1MB single TLS record) via the Redwood agent. 2) Observe repeated TLS handshake stalls when GRE path uses 1400-byte MTU. 3) Repeat during different times — behavior is intermittent depending on ECMP path selection and whether the path's middlebox strips DF bits.
Logs/observations: - Client TLS logs show ClientHello sent, ServerHello not received; TCP retransmits and then eventual timeout.
- tcpdump on node shows ICMP "Fragmentation needed (DF set)" messages from upstream but ICMP are not consistently reaching the source due to NAT and tunneling.
- When forcing PMTU to lower value on the node (e.g., ip route change mtu 1350), downloads succeed.
- Correlation with GRE encapsulation path and a downstream WAN optimizer that rewrites DF/PMTU leading to blackhole for large TLS records.
Initial hypothesis: PMTU discovery/DF-bit handling on the encapsulated GRE path causes large TLS records to be dropped; TLS1.3 ClientHello with extensions (SNI + OCSP stapling) and subsequent record sizes surface the failure. Egress VPCE/Proxy isn't the root cause but amplifies symptom when retried through alternate path.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Customer (ops@maplehealth.com): Noticed about 4% of inference requests fail with timeouts. HTTP 0 on client. Happening since Friday after transit-gw change.

2026-03-10 10:01 - Support (Alex Chen): Requested packet captures and traceroute; asked if customer can reproduce with curl -v against presigned S3 object. Provided temporary debug build that logs TLS handshake timing.
2026-03-10 14:35 - Customer: Uploaded tcpdump and traceroute; confirmed curl -v sometimes hangs with TLS handshake but succeeds when forcing --max-time 30 and reducing MTU locally.

2026-03-11 08:22 - SRE (Priya Raman): Correlated captures with WAN-device vendor; observed ICMP frag-needed from egress side but NAT/TGW drops ICMP responses intermittently. Spun up packet path diagram in Ops channel #private-deploy and notified networking team.
2026-03-12 11:10 - Support: Working on mitigation and will coordinate a temporary PMTU clamp on nodes while vendor investigates GRE DF handling.
2026-03-12 16:40 - Customer: Applied temporary MTU 1350 as requested — artifact pulls succeeded for the past 6 hours with no observed timeouts.
investigation_notes: Checked IP/gre/tunnel MTU settings on affected nodes; default MTU 1500 on inner interface plus GRE overhead leads to 1476 effective path MTU on some paths.
Packet traces show ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed) generated by intermediate router but source address gets rewritten by NAT on TGW causing the original host not to receive it.
Observed correlation between ECMP path selection and failures: when traffic traverses WAN optimizer that strips DF or blocks ICMP, PMTU discovery fails and large TLS records get dropped.
Reproduced locally by forcing DF on large UDP/TCP packets across GRE with controlled middlebox that drops fragments — handshake stalls replicate.

TLS1.3 handshake amplifies the problem because ClientHello size with SNI+OCSP+extensions exceeds the reduced MTU in some cases, causing the initial flight to be dropped rather than retried at a smaller MSS.
No evidence of signature/tls stack bug in Redwood runtime; mitigations focused on networking side (PMTU, MTU clamping, ensure ICMP passthrough).
root_cause: Asymmetric PMTU/DF handling across GRE-encapsulated paths. Middlebox in one ECMP path either drops ICMP Fragmentation Needed messages or rewrites addresses such that PMTU cannot be discovered, creating a blackhole for large TLS records and causing TLS1.3 handshakes to hang intermittently.
resolution: Short-term workaround (applied 2026-03-12): Customer lowered node MTU to 1350 across affected autoscaling group and applied iptables rule to clamp MSS on TCP handshake; artifact/model pulls recovered.
Medium-term action: Coordinate with customer's WAN vendor to ensure ICMP type 3 code 4 is preserved and DF handling is standard on GRE paths. Opened vendor ticket and provided packet captures.

Platform follow-up: Add documentation to Private Deploy runbook about MTU considerations for GRE/IPsec overlays and recommend default MTU clamp when SD-WAN overlays are present. Link to runbook added to related_confluence_pages.
Monitoring: Added alert to Redwood Console route that surfaces increased TLS handshake durations and elevated ICMP frag-needed counts for private deployments.

Status: Workaround in place and customer confirmed recovery; long-term remediation coordinated with customer networking team and vendor. Ticket will be closed after vendor confirms permanent fix and we push runbook updates.
